assigned.title: Search loses text typed before hydration
assigned.acceptance: Text typed into the search field before the form hydrates is not lost: on mount the form adopts the DOM value if it differs from its own state, and a query typed at any point becomes an addressable URL. Proven by an EXECUTED Playwright run on WebKit, where the race reproduces, rather than only on Chromium where it does not. Separately the spec addresses the result heading exactly rather than by substring, because role-name matching is substring by default and a query equal to a title matches both the results heading and the card heading -- a spec defect that only appeared once the suite was first executed.

recommended.title: notFound() never reaches the wire: dead addresses answer 200
recommended.acceptance: An unknown title id and a malformed watch id each answer HTTP 404 rather than a skeleton served at 200, proven by an EXECUTED Playwright run rather than by a route calling notFound(). The cause is that a segment's loading file wraps that segment in Suspense, so React flushes the shell at 200 before the access-fallback error escapes the render and Next can set the status; the root loading file wraps every route in the application, so per-route fixes alone are insufficient. Any fix must keep the loading skeletons rather than deleting them to move a status code. DEPENDS ON PL-0103 because the title route is that task's declared write surface and it is currently in REVIEW; this is a lifecycle dependency, not a technical one.

recommended.title: Catalog metadata source port, and the surfaces still importing the fixture array
recommended.notes: Closes a control-plane gap as well as a code one. The port landed with no task covering it: PL-0104 declares only catalog-card.tsx, routes.ts and routes.test.ts, so apps/web/src/lib/catalog-source.ts, catalog-source-registry.ts, their tests and docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md sat outside every declared surface - unreserved against a parallel writer, and outside any approval fingerprint. This task declares that surface and carries the three import migrations docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md lists as follow-ups. lib/catalog.ts and lib/demo-catalog.ts are reviewDependencies rather than allowedPaths: the port's wiring lives in them and an approval has to bind to it, but they are not this task's to rewrite. The e2e mode split that catalog.api.spec.ts needs once the fixtures stop reaching a production build is deliberately NOT here, because e2e/** belongs to PL-0701; until it lands, that spec fails in the harness's default production mode and .github/workflows/ci.yml says so at the job that runs it.
recommended.acceptance: Discovery reads a metadata port instead of importing a fixture array. catalog-source.ts states the source contract in the published vocabulary - a CatalogItem plus a nullable rights basis - and refuses a record whose basis is undeclared or contradicts its item, by named reason, rather than defaulting either to something permissive; catalog-source-registry.ts is the only module that knows both the port and an implementation, and resolves to not-configured outside the NonDeploymentEnvironment allowlist so the fixtures are unconstructible in a deployment rather than withheld from one; and every remaining surface reads the registry rather than the demoCatalog array - app/search/search.ts, app/title/demo-title-details.ts, and app/api/v1/catalog/home/route.ts, which awaits loadHomeCatalog and maps catalog_source_not_configured onto its own status instead of serving empty rails at 200. When the last surface has moved, the raw demoCatalog export survives only for tests that must be able to name the fixture set, so search and the title page stop being fixture-backed on a build where the home rails are not. docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md stays accurate about what the port still does not solve.
